ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Preventive Visit — David Hume

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Adult preventive visit; no new complaints. [S]

Mr. Hume returns for the preventive visit that was postponed during chemotherapy. He finished his fourth and last cycle of adjuvant CAPOX three and a half weeks ago and was seen nine days ago to begin survivorship surveillance. His September cold cleared within ten days. The fingertip numbness from oxaliplatin is unchanged and does not affect buttoning or writing. His energy is returning; he walks 30 minutes most days and writes every morning. He has regained a little weight. He completed the health risk assessment before the visit. [S]

Adult preventive visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and a written prevention plan given. Depression screen negative; AUDIT-C 4 is a positive screen for unhealthy alcohol use at the threshold for men. [S]
Next preventive visit in one year.

Unhealthy alcohol use, positive screen. About eight to twelve drinks a week. No features of alcohol use disorder. Survivorship guidance advises no more than one drink a day. [S]
Brief counseling given today; he agreed to keep wine to one glass on dinner nights and to have at least three alcohol-free days a week.

Resected stage IIIB colon cancer under surveillance (C18.7). No evidence of recurrence on history or examination; CEA 1.8 ng/mL nine days ago. [S]
Continue the survivorship schedule set at the last visit: CEA and examination in January, CT in December, colonoscopy in June.

Cardiovascular risk. LDL cholesterol 118 mg/dL, total cholesterol 196, HDL 52, blood pressure 122/74, non-smoker, no diabetes (HbA1c 5.5%). Estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk about 10 percent, without dyslipidemia, diabetes, hypertension, or smoking. [S]
Shared decision: he prefers diet and activity first; less red meat and pastry, more vegetables and whole grains, which also fits his survivorship plan.
Recheck lipids in one year.

text.paragraph: Immunizations given today: Influenza vaccine, 2026-2027 season; Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine PCV20 [S]

Guideline basis: Medicare Preventive Services reference: visit templates, screening cascades, and documentation elements (2026); USPSTF A and B Recommendations (2026); Adult Immunization Schedule by Age, United States, 2025 (2025)
Follow-up: Hepatitis C and HIV tests with the next blood draw. CT in December. Surveillance visit with CEA and the first zoster vaccine dose in January. Next preventive visit in one year. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent, prompted by his cancer diagnosis. He has named a health care agent and completed a written health care directive, now scanned into the chart. If the cancer recurs, he wants a frank account of the options and their expected benefit, and he would accept surgery or chemotherapy that offered a real chance of cure or of more good time. He would not want resuscitation or prolonged life support if recovery to independent life and work were not expected, and he would want comfort-focused care at home at the end of life. [S]
